title: Finite-presentation module, morphism and equality descent over arbitrary qcqs affine-transition limits
statement:
Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with affine transition morphisms $p_{ji}:S_j\to S_i$ for $j\geq i$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Assume every $S_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and let $S=\varprojlim_i S_i$ with projections $p_i$ be its scheme limit: $p_{ji}\circ p_j=p_i$ for $j\geq i$, and every compatible family $t_i:T\to S_i$ from a scheme $T$ factors uniquely as $t_i=p_i\circ t$ through a morphism $t:T\to S$. For sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], finite presentation means that every point has an open neighbourhood $U$ on which there is an exact sequence $\mathcal O_U^m\to\mathcal O_U^n\to F|_U\to0$ for finite $m,n$. Use tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] throughout, identifying iterated pullbacks by its canonical composition isomorphisms. Then:
(1) Every finitely presented $\mathcal O_S$-module $F$ admits a finitely presented $\mathcal O_{S_i}$-module $F_i$ at some $i$, with $p_i^*F_i\cong F$.
(2) For any $i$, finitely presented $\mathcal O_{S_i}$-modules $F_i,G_i$ and a morphism $u:p_i^*F_i\to p_i^*G_i$, there are $j\geq i$ and $u_j:p_{ji}^*F_i\to p_{ji}^*G_i$ whose pullback to $S$ equals $u$ through the canonical composition isomorphisms.
(3) For any $i$, finitely presented $\mathcal O_{S_i}$-modules $F_i,G_i$ and morphisms $u_i,v_i:F_i\to G_i$ with $p_i^*u_i=p_i^*v_i$, there is $j\geq i$ such that $p_{ji}^*u_i=p_{ji}^*v_i$.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover $\{U_a\}$ of $S$. For every nonempty pairwise intersection and triple intersection choose finite affine charts $W_{ab,r}$ and $T_{abc,s}$; choose finite affine charts on each overlap $W_{ab,r}\cap W_{ab,r'}$, and refine the triple charts so that each lies in the three relevant pair charts. Apply [lem-trf-affine-open-limit-descent] to this finite list and pass, by directedness, to one stage containing all the resulting stage opens. The restricted systems have affine transitions and the asserted limits by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-cone-affine-projections-opens].

source.place: Tag 01ZR, first proof: reduce to the affine case and use Zariski gluing; Tags 01Z4 and 01YW for finite affine charts

proof.text: All chosen opens and their finite intersections are quasi-compact: the descended charts are affine, and intersections of finitely many affine opens are quasi-compact in the quasi-separated stages. For each chart, parent intersection, and incidence inclusion, first descend the relevant quasi-compact intersection by clause (1) of [pqf-lem-limit-qc-open-descends]. Its inverse image in $S$ agrees with the corresponding limit intersection. Apply clause (2) of that node to the two descended opens with equal inverse images; after enlargement their stage opens are equal, which gives the desired inclusion. Apply the same argument to the finite lists of parent charts, pair refinements and triple refinements, and take one common upper bound. Then the finite unions equal the corresponding stage intersections, and the finite union of the $U_a$ equals the whole stage. Thus every chart and refinement covers the actual stage open, and [lem-weil-pbc-limit-global-sections-colimit] gives the filtered-colimit description of every chart and refinement ring.

source.place: Tag 01ZR, first proof: finite affine charts and Zariski gluing

proof.text: On each affine limit chart $U_a$, $W_{ab,r}$ and $T_{abc,s}$, finite presentation implies quasi-coherence and the restriction has a finitely presented module of sections by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine]. The comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections-bijective] and the affine tilde/global-sections equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identify restriction and tensor pullback with extension of scalars. Using the colimit rings of Steps 1--2, [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] descends all local modules and every canonical comparison map to one common stage.

source.place: Tag 01ZR, first proof: affine case via Algebra, Lemma 05N7

proof.text: For every pair chart, the canonical comparison on the limit is an isomorphism. After the map descent in Step 3, descend its inverse as a second map between the same finitely presented stage modules using the map clause of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine]. Enlarge once more so that both composites of the descended map and descended inverse equal the relevant identity: their pullbacks to $S$ are identities, and the equality clause of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] applies to this finite list. Hence every descended comparison $\theta_{ab,r}$ is an isomorphism, with a specified descended inverse, before any gluing is performed.

source.place: Tag 01ZR, first proof: affine case via Algebra, Lemma 05N7 and Zariski gluing

proof.text: On each affine refinement of $W_{ab,r}\cap W_{ab,r'}$, the pullbacks of the two pair-chart comparisons agree because both are the canonical comparison for $F$. Apply the equality clause of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] to this finite family and pass to a common later stage. The comparisons therefore agree on every actual pair-chart overlap by Step 2; their descended inverses agree there as well, since composing either inverse with the common isomorphism gives the same identity. Thus the $\theta_{ab,r}$ glue to one isomorphism on each full stage intersection $U_a\cap U_b$.

source.place: Tag 01ZR, first proof: Zariski gluing of the affine case

proof.text: On every refined triple chart $T_{abc,s}$, form the two composites of the three transition isomorphisms, using the canonical iterated-pullback identifications. Their pullbacks to $S$ agree with the third transition map by functoriality of the canonical comparison for $F$; the identity equations on repeated indices similarly pull back to identities. Apply the equality clause of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] to this finite list and enlarge once so that all cocycle and identity equations hold on the stage. Because the triple refinements cover each full triple intersection by Step 2, the glued transition isomorphisms satisfy the fpqc descent cocycle everywhere.

source.place: Tag 01ZR, clause (1) and first proof, Zariski gluing

proof.text: The stage opens $U_a$ are a finite jointly surjective cover by Step 2; as affine open immersions they form an fpqc covering. The isomorphisms from Steps 4--6 are defined on all pairwise intersections and satisfy the cocycle on all triple intersections. Therefore [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] glues them to a quasi-coherent module $F_i$; its finite-presentation preservation/reflection clause gives finite presentation. The local identifications pull back to $S$ and agree on every pair chart, so they glue to $p_i^*F_i\cong F$. This proves clause (1).

source.place: Tag 01ZR, first proof: Zariski gluing of the affine case

proof.text: For clause (2), restrict $u:p_i^*F_i\to p_i^*G_i$ to the finite cover $U_a$. The affine comparisons identify these restrictions with module maps, and the map clause of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] lifts every restriction to a common later stage. On each pair refinement, the two local lifts have equal pullback to $S$; its equality clause makes them equal after a further enlargement. The pair refinements cover each full intersection by Step 2, so the lifts glue by [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] to a global $u_j$ whose pullback is $u$.

source.place: Tag 01ZR, clause (2) and first proof, affine case plus Zariski gluing

proof.text: For clause (3), restrict $u_i$ and $v_i$ to the same finite cover. Their pulled-back affine module maps agree over $S$, so the equality clause of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] gives a later stage where they agree on every $U_a$ after one common upper bound. Since the $U_a$ cover that stage by Step 2, faithfulness in [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] implies $p_{ji}^*u_i=p_{ji}^*v_i$ globally.

source.place: Tag 01ZR, clause (3) and first proof, affine case plus Zariski gluing
